messages:
incident-bot: Pager — high p95 latency + 503s on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 (alerts: latency > 1200ms, error rate > 2%)
Alex M.: I picked this up — seeing a spike in queue depth on the EU batchers and a handful of nodes reporting OOM-ish GC pauses. Metrics pasted below.
Priya K.: link to dashboards: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/egress-eu?range=1h — p95 jumped from 220ms -> 1.6s at 09:12 UTC.
Mateo R.: Noticed increased request fanout to model-small-quant due to routing policy change earlier. Could be a cold-cache ripple.
Jin L.: Replaying logs, I see repeated `kv_cache.miss -> fetch model shard` patterns and slow network to redis-eu-2: `tcp retransmit` spikes.
Sara T.: Customer impact: two enterprise tenants reported intermittent 503s for about 25 minutes. CS flagged them. No billing impact yet.
Alex M.: Current status: throttled the EU batcher ingress by 30% (soft limit), enabled fallback routing to eu-west-2 for low-priority traffic. This reduced queue depth.
Priya K.: Actions taken (timeline):
 - 09:12 UTC: incident-bot alert
 - 09:14 UTC: Alex applied soft-throttle on batcher (route policy: `eu-priority -> eu2-fallback`)
 - 09:18 UTC: Jin confirmed redis-eu-2 p95 write latency spike; escalated to infra team
 - 09:22 UTC: Mateo changed model routing to prefer `model-small-quant-v2` to reduce mem pressure
 - 09:28 UTC: observed stabilization of p95 to ~300ms
Mateo R.: Quick note: the routing change that bumped traffic to `model-small-quant` was from a canary rollout (traffic steering) — canary config was changed at 08:50 UTC by release-bot.
Alex M.: Who's taking primary for the remainder of the shift? I'm handing primary to @Priya for the next 4 hours. @Jin you're secondary unless you want to swap.
Priya K.: I'll own primary. I'll keep the throttle in place for another hour and monitor. Jin L. I'll ping you for infra escalations.
Jin L.: Affirmative. I'll follow up with infra on redis-eu-2 net flaps and request packet captures.
Sara T.: I'll coordinate with CS — sending summary to affected customers and offering status update. Draft: "We're seeing elevated latencies in EU; traffic has been redirected and mitigations are in place. We'll update once stable."
Alex M.: Runbook pointers: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batcher-throttle and https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fallback — key steps followed are in the 'soft-throttle' checklist.
Priya K.: Current investigation items for the handoff:
 - Confirm infra root cause for redis-eu-2 (Jin)
 - Verify whether canary rollout at 08:50 should be rolled back (Mateo)
 - Confirm no long-tail customer retries caused duplicate load (Alex)
 - Postmortem owner assignment (TBD)
Alex M.: Next steps for Priya (in order):
 1) Keep throttle for 1h, watch p95 and error rate dash
 2) If p95 < 400ms for next 30m, gradually restore throttle by 10% every 10m
 3) If error rate creeps >1% again, trigger full fallback to eu-west-2 for non-SLA traffic
 4) File incident ticket in Jira: INC- (I'll create and assign)
Priya K.: I'll also add a quick eval of model choices to see if the memory footprint of the canary variant is higher than expected.
Mateo R.: For the RCA: early hypothesis is compounded — canary routing change + intermittent redis net issues -> backlog -> batcher memory pressure -> GC pauses -> client timeouts.
Jin L.: Logging notes: captured tcpdump snippet and increased debug on redis client for next 2 hours. I'll attach to the incident ticket.
Sara T.: CS notified customers at 09:45 UTC. I'll post the canned update in #customers-affected and tag account reps.
Alex M.: Handoff checklist completed: primary reassigned, mitigations in place, infra engagement opened, CS notified.
Priya K.: I'll post a 1hr update here and close this thread when stabilization is confirmed. Please add any loose threads. :thumbsup:
Mateo R.: Added note to rollback canary if infra confirms persistent network instability.
Jin L.: Will follow up with infra within 30m.
incident-bot: Incident ticket created INC-3429, Pager duty entries logged, runbook steps recorded.
Alex M.: Thanks team — leaving notes for postmortem: timeline, canary config diff, redis metrics, batcher memory graphs, customer impact summary.
Priya K.: Copy. Handoff recorded. I'll update last_message_ts when I close.
